_meta.source: Teks asli heartodex (descriptionOriginal di file data) dengan salah ketik yang jelas dibetulkan. descriptionOriginal tetap apa adanya.

schneider: It's merely an easygoing, beautiful little fish. It never fights or competes, always waiting for food to swim into its mouth.
common-bleak: With its mouth turned up so high, is it angry at someone?
barbel: Barbel refers to both the fish and the whisker-like sensory organ. Naming can be oddly lazy sometimes.
common-chub: It prefers to stay in lakes that hardly flow. Its nature seems just as laid-back.
oriental-shrimp: It's commonly found in rivers and often slips into waterweeds to shield itself from the sun.
common-prawn: Marine shrimp—regulars at the dinner table.
crucian-carp: It's said that a young crucian carp begins life with a vibrant golden sheen, though the color gradually dulls as it matures.
common-whitefish: It has a slender body and won't move easily once it finds a place it likes.
sea-stickleback: Don't be fooled by its tiny size. To plankton and small fry, it's actually a deadly predator.
scad: This small and agile fish shares its home with Jellyfish.
skipjack-tuna: Those small bumps behind the dorsal fin are "hidden thrusters" for speed swimmers.
spined-loach: This slender fish startles easily. Be gentle when fishing to avoid spooking it.
sea-bass: It lives in coastal waters, boasting tender and juicy flesh.
european-perch: Widely found in freshwater, it's common yet delicious. Most people must have eaten it.
streber: It's a special kind of freshwater perch with big blocks of dark blue speckles.
minnow: It's a slender fish with delicate scales.
beltfish: Its slim body flows like white silk through the currents.
striped-red-mullet: It has two long chin barbels that resemble an elderly goat, full of wisdom.
sardine: It's a small, pale fish commonly found in the sea.
tench: Rumor has it these slippery fish can heal each other by body-touching, thus the nickname "Doctor Fish."
seahorse: It's quirky yet beautiful, also sluggish.
european-smelt: It tastes like fresh cucumbers. A female smelt can produce tens of thousands of eggs.
false-scad: It's often confused with scad due to similar appearance, but they share no relation.
largemouth-bass: This carnivorous fish is known for its ferocity. It often hides among waterweeds and strikes when prey passes by.
stone-loach: Its sleek body slips easily through sand and gravel. When startled, it quickly clamps onto the rock.
anglerfish: A female anglerfish has a little lantern hanging on the head, a well-crafted bait.
common-octopus: It's a mid-sized octopus and a light chaser in the sea.
atlantic-pygmy-octopus: Sure, it's mini-sized, but calling it a "pygmy" is a bit too much!
turbot: It's a type of flatfish. While its appearance may not be ideal, it's one of the gentle guys.
hermit-crab: Who says rent is obligatory? Not the hermit crab, an expert at claiming new shells.
european-crayfish: Protected by a tough exoskeleton and massive pincers, this crayfish never backs down from a threat.
zander: It's a meat lover, so it tends to gain weight easily.
ruffe: It's a carnivorous fish that prefers warm lakes.
mud-sunfish: Muddy-colored fish muddle in murky lake mud. Well, that doesn't roll off the tongue quite well.
clownfish: Lively and adorable, it rose to fame in the aquatic world thanks to a role in a certain ocean-themed blockbuster.
edible-frog: Its ancestor is the pond frog and marsh frog, widely distributed across lakes.
atlantic-salmon: It's one of the common members of the salmon family, known for its nutritious orange flesh that is delicious whether raw or cooked.
tilapia: For its deliciousness, some call it white salmon.
river-crab: It prefers meat and will break it down with its pincers and eat it piece by piece. Elegance.
common-carp: It's full of energy and strength that leaps to escape when hooked. Don't let it slip away!
butterfly-koi: A graceful "water fairy," pure and floating, but highly sensitive and needs careful care.
burbot: It has a short barbel on the chin, which serves as an organ for detecting scents.
mussel: It has a tough shell with green and yellow bands, and its flesh is highly nutritious.
goby: It forms a disc-shaped sucker with its pelvic fins to stick to rocks and stay anchored against flowing currents.
red-bellied-piranha: Its red belly is natural—no, it wasn't burned.
european-plaice: A fish that forages only at night, with just enough eyesight to get by.
rabbit-fish: Viewed from above, it resembles a graceful butterfly with a tail, but its dorsal spine is mildly poisonous.
tadpole: It's tiny and unremarkable at first, then becomes a frog by summer... if it survives.
freshwater-blenny: There are two tiny flowers on its head, swaying gently with the current.
atlantic-mackerel: It's stoic, rare, and beautiful, but it really likes to sleep more than it should.
european-flying-squid: It uses jet propulsion and fin vibrations to "fly" for short distances, hence the name "flying squid."
european-lobster: It's a larger species of lobster, and its two massive claws look quite menacing.
common-rudd: Red eyes... did someone make him cry?
trout: It has an alluring coloration and prefers to live in relatively cold lakes.
large-pearl-mussel: This shellfish, lying motionless at the bottom of the lake, cannot excrete the indigestible foreign matter in its body, so it can only wrap it up into pearls.
puffer-fish: It's a diadromous fish, though it spends most of the time in saltwater.
tub-gurnard: The orange-red scales on its back create a beautiful sight.
chum-salmon: As it matures, it changes colors and becomes a fish of fashion.
nursehound: Its eyes glow at night due to reflected light, just like cats.
grayling: Its scales refract a dreamy purple hue, making it quite suitable as an aquarium fish.
european-eel: A deep-sea marathoner that can migrate thousands of miles without eating.
blackspot-seabream: It roams the deeper reaches of the sea with ease.
mediterranean-killifish: It's covered in dark stripes, and its dream is to live a peaceful life.
three-spined-stickleback: When fighting, the three spines on its body erect to intimidate opponents.
giant-oarfish: Some call it an emissary of the dragon palace, others say it's a deep-sea demon. Its behavior remains unknown.
mottled-sculpin: It usually stays at the bottom of the water, too lazy to swim around.
king-crab: Its tender flesh is rich in various proteins and healthy fats. Best steamed.
golden-king-crab: This giant sea crab, with its massive body and spiny shell, has been the inspiration for countless horror films.
blue-european-crayfish: The shell has mutated into a light blue color, but it's still a freshwater crayfish at heart.
haddock: Prefers to stay still on the shallow seafloor, but will roam around when foraging.
goldfish: With dazzling colors and graceful posture, it's the beauty pageant champion of the fish world.
european-mudminnow: It prefers to hide at the bottom of lakes. Its dark brown speckles help it blend seamlessly into the surroundings.
bluefin-tuna: Born with restless energy, it can swim swiftly in the deep sea.
northern-pike: Its appetite matches its large size. Leftover food on its teeth is eaten later like snacks.
moonfish: Round like the Mid-Autumn Festival moon, it moves in the same cycle—hiding deep by day and rising to shallower waters by night.
ocean-sunfish: With a large head and stubby tail, its odd shape earned it the nickname "swimming head."
pumpkinseed: It's covered in many green and blue speckles, like wearing clothes with glowing spots.
huchen: He eats meat and grows strong. He is a lone wolf.
swordfish: It has an iconic sword-like rostrum, making it the swimming champion of the fish world.
wels-catfish: This freshwater fish has a long lifespan that lives up to several decades.
bluegill: It's a rare species that can thrive in warm lakes. Doesn't it worry about cooking itself?
shortfin-mako-shark: Its tail fin has a distinctive crescent shape, like a moon in the water
smooth-hammerhead: It has a head shaped like a hammer. With sharp teeth and swift movements, it's a ferocious hunter in the sea.
arctic-char: Covered in red sparkles, it's a fearless fish that braves cold weather
golden-garfish: Golden from head to tail, this garfish is a rare sight-definitely worth showing off if you reel one in.
pale-gold-garfish: A living fossil of the fish world, its pale gold skin makes it look surprisingly young.
brown-garfish: Plain on the outside, but a ruthless hunter. Even its eggs are highly toxic.
black-garfish: The black stripes alone are enough to make it look intimidating. And when it hunts? It goes after just about anything that swims.
silver-garfish: Its silver-white sheen looks like something that swam right out of a moonbeam. And those red eyes? Pure mystery.
japanese-flying-squid: A relentless hustler living life at full speed-eats just about anything.
firefly-squid: The bioluminescent firefly squid-like a meteor shower deep in the sea.
sea-slug: Looks soft and squishy like candy, but many types are actually super toxic-better not touch.
mandarin-fish: Dressed in an iridescent maze pattern, but extremely picky about what it eats.
oliver-ridley-turtle: The species' survival strategy? Overwhelm everything with sheer numbers-the "turtle-wave tactic."
flatback-turtle: A sea turtle that sticks to the coast, with a shell as flat as its name suggests.
scallop: The swimming champion of the shellfish world.
blue-brick-clownfish: A blue toy clownfish made of bricks. Might be too childish for kids, but just right for adults.
colorful-brick-clownfish: A colorful toy clownfish made of bricks—pretty hard on the eyes to put together.
purple-brick-clownfish: A purple toy clownfish made of bricks. Does it blow bubbles when it swims?
red-brick-clownfish: The most true-to-life brick toy of the sea's biggest star—reportedly a perennial bestseller.
green-brick-clownfish: A green toy clownfish made of bricks. Well, its "eye-friendly" selling point is now out the window.
director-common-octopus-w-cinnamon-hat: A toy Common Octopus in a cinnamon director hat, capable of multitasking at least eight things at once.
director-common-octopus-w-patterned-hat: A toy Common Octopus in a patterned director hat, whose keen sense of light allows it to precisely control the set's lighting.
director-pygmy-octopus-w-cyan-hat: A toy Pygmy Octopus in a cyan director hat. Its shell-hiding nature gives it a unique perspective on filmmaking.
director-pygmy-octopus-w-navy-hat: A toy Pygmy Octopus in a navy director hat, convinced it excels at ocean-adventure films.
director-pygmy-octopus-w-brown-hat: A toy Pygmy Octopus in a brown director hat. Every thriller shoot is a huge challenge for this timid creature.
frostspore-seahorse: A Frostspore Seahorse drifting leisurely in the water looks just like a beautiful ice sculpture.
frostspore-king-crab: A king crab infected by Frostspore, its sharp, aloof stance making it even more regal.
frostspore-puffer-fish: A Frostspore-infected puffer fish looks a bit more slender—is this the so-called thermal contraction?
frostspore-ocean-sunfish: With such a big, heavy Frostspore head, doesn't it just plunge straight to the bottom?
frostspore-whale-shark: When a whale shark gets infected by frostspore, the little fish that usually hitch rides on it get very sad.
